explanations.31: This stores multiple engagement types (likes, reposts, comments) for one person using a Set, so we can easily check if they engaged in multiple ways.
explanations.79: This type says an embed is either an external link card, an image gallery, or something else we don't recognize — the last option catches unknown Bluesky embed types.
explanations.86: The author object must have a displayName here (not optional), even though the BlueskyActor type normally allows it to be missing.
explanations.98: This nested function walks through a tree structure of replies to collect all the people who commented, including replies to replies.
explanations.119: This inner function is a helper that records an engagement action for one person, but skips the blog owner's own account since that's not real reader engagement.
explanations.138: This sorts people by how many different ways they engaged (liked AND reposted ranks higher than just liked), putting the most engaged readers first.
explanations.143: This removes query parameters from a URL and trailing slashes, so different links to the same article are recognized as the same.
explanations.156: If the cached data is older than the TTL (time-to-live), we treat it as expired and fetch fresh data instead.
explanations.209: If there's a cursor from the previous API response, we add it to request the next page of results — this is how pagination works with the Bluesky API.
explanations.222: The exclamation mark tells TypeScript we're certain this will have a value, because we just checked that the post URI exists and it always has at least one slash.
explanations.263: This flag prevents updating state after the component unmounts — if the user navigates away before the fetch finishes, we ignore the result.
explanations.269: We only update state if the fetch wasn't cancelled, because if the user navigated to a different article, this stale result is no longer relevant.
explanations.309: This uses type casting to narrow the union type — we tell TypeScript which response shape we got based on which list key we're looking for.
explanations.354: This constructs the Bluesky URI format, which uses the account handle and post ID to uniquely identify the post.
explanations.375: We only call the expensive APIs if there are actually likes or reposts to fetch — if the counts are zero, we skip the network request and use empty arrays.
explanations.380: This merges the previously fetched commenters with the newly fetched likers and reposters, recalculating the ranking since we now have more data.
